Highlights at a glance
One Roll, Any Post: The flexible mesh tensions onto wooden posts, steel T posts or concrete pillars without special fixings, so you can use the posts and stirrup wire you already own. A two person crew can unroll, tension and tie a paddock in a fraction of the time rigid panels demand, and there is no on site welding anywhere in the job. Standard hand tools, a strainer and a pair of pliers, are enough to finish the job.
Follows The Land: Slopes, gullies and curved field edges break rigid fence, but a flexible roll bends with the ground while keeping even spacing between posts. Rolling terrain stops being a reason to order a custom job, because the mesh simply follows the contour and the tension does the rest. Uneven ground installs become a one day task instead of a week of cutting, fitting and rework.
Light To Move, Fast To Start: The roll format keeps 164ft of fence in a compact coil that loads in a pickup bed or on a hand cart, so distant paddocks are reachable without machinery. Crews carry several rolls at once and start fencing wherever the animals actually are, rather than hauling long rigid panels that need a trailer and extra hands at every corner of the field.
Repairs Without Experts: When a tree limb or vehicle damages one section, you re tension the affected span instead of replacing a whole panel. Individual stays can be retied and the line wire re strained with basic fencing tools, which keeps a working boundary working while a proper fix is scheduled. The gap between damage and repair is where most livestock losses and headaches happen.
Posts Follow The Farm: Because the mesh adapts to post spacing on gentle ground, you can set posts where soil and water points demand and let the fence adjust to them. Rigid systems force post positions to match panel widths, which often means extra digging and concrete. With a roll, the layout follows the farm, and that flexibility becomes saved labor and saved posts on every kilometer fenced.

Ball Containment: Fine mesh cells stop balls from escaping the playing area, so games continue without constant retrieval stops and neighbors stay clear of stray shots. Fast Perimeter Build: Rolls unroll along posts, tension with rail and tension wire, then fix with clips for a straight run that follows the court outline precisely. Crews cover long perimeters quickly because the fabric needs no panel alignment, and damaged sections later are cut out and rewoven rather than ordering a full new panel run for one bad spot.
